At the marked, best and last checkpoints

Each row reads the evaluation at exactly that step (the final checkpoint, saved after the last evaluation, reads the last one). The counts are episodes of that evaluation: over pad bar, over tilt bar and over lift bar count full-horizon episodes whose own rail value exceeds the stage's bar; outside band and outside pad band count full-horizon episodes with either foot's window-mean CoP outside the band's edges; flagged by actuator counts the saturation-flagged episodes by the actuator each names and its sign (+ every saturated step at +1, - at -1, +/- both), so the final, best and robust_best checkpoints are read from their own evaluation's rows. The rail and saturation-fraction columns are the mean and the worst full-horizon episode. CoP in half-lengths (+ toe), tilt in degrees, lift in mm, left minus right in degrees (hip roll: each leg + abduction), the head tip in m (its window mean, and the lowest episode's window minimum), the neck and head pitch in degrees (+ nose down), std in action units at the checkpoint saved at that step. judge joint and judge own are the judge's joint-space and own-sigma noise falls (of 20) at a checkpoint judged at exactly that step, from the judge files named for the run: a readout, never a verdict.

What these pages do not show

  • Hip roll and head posture: recorded per episode (<foot>_hip_roll_mean_deg, <foot>_hip_roll_max_abs_deg, head_tip_height_mean_m, head_tip_height_min_m, neck_pitch_mean_deg, head_pitch_mean_deg) only in ledgers written since those columns were added; an older run's are absent series. The left-minus-right hip roll is each episode's left leg's mean minus its right leg's, both + abduction. A model without a head-tip site or a neck or head pitch hinge reads nan there, and a model without a box-soled foot records none (its evaluation runs no recorder). No gate reads them.
  • The evaluation episodes are the deterministic policy's, at yaw 0 on the evaluation env's own resets. The judge's perturbation panels (its joint-noise falls, K3) and its verdicts are not in these files: the outcomes page draws K3's inputs only from the judge files a caller names (--judged; the stance3, stance4, stance5 and stance5 replication judges' files, whose K3 is the same), as a readout of the stance5 replication judge's K3 criterion, never a verdict. The training falls are the stochastic training policy's.
  • The saturating actuator and the saturation fraction itself are recorded per episode (saturated_actuator, saturated_actuator_fraction) only in ledgers written since those columns were added; an older run's are absent series, and its screen_v2_reasons lists max_actuator_saturation_fraction without naming the actuator. An episode names one actuator, the lowest index on a tie (saturated_actuator_ties counts the others); the other actuators that saturated are counted (actuators_saturated), not named.
  • The CoP band is paid per window step on each loaded foot's CoP; these files keep each episode's window mean per foot only, so the outside-band count reads that mean against the band's edges.
  • The commanded leg offsets (leg_dc_*) and the per-foot heel moment margin (<foot>_heel_margin_nm) are kept in gate_progress.npz only, not in eval_episodes.csv.
  • Per-actuator std is read at the checkpoints kept in models/ only; between them nothing is recorded here (policy_probe.npz holds it per update where the run kept that file; the exploration page reads it there).
  • The body columns (commands, tail and body posture, energy, drift and slip, joint stops, the centre of mass and momentum, base wrenches, head rate) are recorded per episode only in ledgers written since they were added; an older run's are absent series, and a model without a part (no tail, no neck) reads nan there. The K3 noise panel is in the stage directory only where the launch enabled it (k3_panel.json); the judge's own K3 is in its files (--judged). The normalization page reads the VecNormalize pickles kept in models/ only.
  • The per-rollout clip shares are the training rollouts' (sampled actions, and the policy's means at the same observations), from policy_probe.npz only where the run kept it and wrote its rollout_* arrays; an older run's are absent series. The JSON keeps each actuator's peak and last values; the per-rollout series are in the file.

How the numbers are reduced

  • counts: episodes, full_horizon, falls (shorter than the horizon), clean and saturated over all the evaluation's episodes; clean and saturated over the episodes the screen judged
  • columns: each per-episode column's mean, std (ddof 0), min, max and n over the evaluation's full-horizon episodes
  • over_bar: <rail>_over_bar: the evaluation's full-horizon episodes whose own <rail> value (the episode's maximum over the feet; for the CoP rails the window mean of |CoP| with an unloaded step counted as 1) exceeds the stage's declared bar; <rail>_over_bar_fraction: that count over the full-horizon episodes that measured the rail
  • outside_band: foot_cop_outside_band (sole_cop_outside_pad_band): the evaluation's full-horizon episodes with either foot's window-mean whole-foot (pad) CoP outside the band's edges, an unloaded foot not counted; the edges are the run's own or, where it records none, the reference edges band_edges_source names
  • saturation: an evaluation is flagged when >= 5 of its episodes list max_actuator_saturation_fraction in screen_v2_reasons (the scorers' rule, set on 10-episode evaluations); 2 flagged evaluations in a row (adjacent evaluations) are an alarm, raised at evaluation 2 of the run
  • flagged_actuators: per evaluation, the saturation-flagged episodes (as counted for saturated) by the actuator each names: eval_episodes.csv's saturated_actuator, the actuator with the largest fraction of post-settle window steps at |action| >= 0.99 (the lowest index on a tie), with its sign: + when every one of its saturated steps was commanded positive, - when none was, +/- when both; (unmeasured) an unmeasured window, (not recorded) a row written before the column. Each alarm lists the counts over its flagged evaluations and names the actuator most of them name, counted over its signs (a named actuator before (unmeasured) and (not recorded), then the first by name, on a tie), with the sign most of its episodes carry (+/- on a tie)
  • training_falls: train_episodes.csv episodes whose cause is not truncated, per window of 262,144 steps (k w, (k + 1) w]; the last window ends at its last episode
  • rollout_shares: from policy_probe.npz, per training rollout (the buffer the next PPO update trains on, read before it) and per actuator: action_clip_high_share and action_clip_low_share, the sampled actions above the action space's high bound and below its low one (env.step clips them; the buffer keeps them unclipped); action_saturated_share, the clipped sample at |action| >= 0.99; mu_beyond_high_share and mu_beyond_low_share, the policy's mean action at the same observations beyond each bound; mu_mean, mu_q50 and mu_q95, that mean's average, median and 95th percentile. Each actuator's peak share and its values at the last measured rollout; first_at_level, the first rollout whose share at either bound reaches level; named, the (actuator, bound) series the pages draw by name (at most 6, the highest peak first). Never smoothed
  • posture: head_tip_height_mean_m and head_tip_height_min_m: each episode's post-settle window mean and minimum of the head tip's height (m above z = 0); neck_pitch_mean_deg and head_pitch_mean_deg: the window means of the neck's pitch (its pitch hinges summed) and the head's, from home, + nose down; <foot>_hip_roll_mean_deg: the window mean of the leg's hip roll from home, + abduction on either side, and <foot>_hip_roll_max_abs_deg its window maximum of |angle from home|; left-minus-right hip roll: per episode, the left leg's mean minus the right's. Reduced like every other column; no gate reads them
  • judge_k3: from the judge files named per run (--judged): per judged checkpoint, the joint-space noise falls (noise_matched_control_joint) and the own-sigma falls (noise_matched_own) of the judge's 20 episodes, against the stance5 replication judge's K3 (docs/investigations/stance_2026_10/stance5/replication/criteria.txt: K3, robustness at 6,291,456 and at final: joint-space noise falls at most 2 of 20, and own-sigma falls at most 1 of 20; the same K3 as stance3's, stance4's and stance5's). Files of those judges only (stance3-judge/v1, stance4-judge/v1, stance5-judge/v1, stance5r-judge/v1); within_bar at K3's checkpoints only, withheld (null) where a panel is not 20 episodes on spawns 3042-3061. A readout of the judge's records, never a verdict: the scorer decides whether a run holds
  • body: the body columns of eval_episodes.csv (gait.body_telemetry): each actuator's window-mean command, the at-rail and parked actuators (rail_named, parked_named: per evaluation, the full-horizon episodes by actuator and sign; rail_episodes, parked_episodes: those with any), the tail's hinges and chord, the root's height, pitch and roll, the mechanical work, peak power, torque and command jitter per actuator group, the drift, path, yaw and slip, the joint stops, the centre of mass's and capture point's margins, the centroidal angular momentum, the tail-base and neck-base wrench and the head's rate; reduced like every other column. Report only; no gate reads them
  • k3_panel: from the stage's k3_panel.json (k3_panel.py, enabled at launch): per panel rolled during training on the live policy, the own-sigma and joint-space falls of its episodes with the stance5 replication judge's arithmetic; within_bar at K3's checkpoints only (6,291,456 and the final panel), withheld where a panel is not 20 episodes on spawns 3042-3061; a series never joins two joint sigmas. A readout, never a verdict: the offline judge's K3 is the K3 of record
  • exploration: the leg actuators' exp(log_std) from policy_probe.npz (every PPO update), else from the checkpoint zips; leg_std_at_k3: each leg actuator's std at the last update at or before each K3 point; the reference 0.08 is the stance3 design's line-2 floor, not applied
  • obs_normalization: per periodic and final VecNormalize pickle (read through a stub unpickler: numpy's array helpers and inert stand-ins only), per observation dimension: shift = (mean_k - mean_ref) / sqrt(var_ref + eps) and scale = 0.5 ln((var_k + eps) / (var_ref + eps)) against the checkpoint before (_prev) and the final pickle (_final), their max and median over the dimensions; the probe bank's statue_settled row's clipped normalized value's change between checkpoints; the probe's float32 rows against the pickles at shared steps
  • comparison_smoothing_evaluations: 5
  • comparison_smoothing: comparisons draw the continuous series as a centred rolling mean over that many evaluations, each evaluation's value faint behind it; counts are never smoothed
  • numbers: six significant digits; null where not measured
